name: Texprove WF2 - Compliance check and draft

parameters.text:
=Write a short first-contact B2B email from {{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Sender Name'] }}, {{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Sender Title'] }} at Texprove to {{ $json['Contact Name'] }} ({{ $json['Contact Title'] }}) at {{ $json.Company }}.
Language: Turkish if Language = tr, otherwise English; write natural business Turkish, not a translation. This lead's Language is: {{ $json.Language }}.
Greeting: if the Contact Name above is a real person's name, greet that person (Turkish: "Sayın" + full name; English: "Dear" + full name). If the Contact Name is empty, or is a job title, role or placeholder rather than a person's name (for example "General Manager", "Export Contact", "Sales Team", or anything containing "/"), greet the company instead: English "Dear {{ $json.Company }} team,", Turkish "Sayın {{ $json.Company }} ekibi,". Never use a job title or role as the greeting.
Open with this verified fact: {{ $json['Personalisation Hook'] }}.
Explain in one sentence that EU Digital Product Passport rules for textiles are coming and exporters to the EU will need product-level data. One sentence on how Texprove helps. Ask for a 15-minute call.
Max 120 words for the main text, no hype, no attachments. The only links allowed are the recipient company's own website and Texprove's website in the signature.
Never mention the company's customers, buyers or the brands or retailers it supplies, nor any order volumes, quantities, prices, capacities, margins or revenue, even if that information is public. If the verified fact contains such details, refer to it in general terms (for example "your exports to European retailers").
End with the sender's full name ({{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Sender Name'] }}), title ({{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Sender Title'] }}), company legal name ({{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Company Legal Name'] }}), address ({{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Company Address'] }}) and website ({{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Company Website'] || 'https://www.texprove.com' }}), each on its own line, exactly as given.
Then add this sentence saying where we found their details, in the email's language, exactly as given:
Turkish: İletişim bilgilerinizi şirketinizin herkese açık web sitesinden aldık.
English: We found your contact details on your company's public website.
Then this opt-out line, in the email's language, exactly as given:
Turkish: {{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Opt-out TR'] }}
English: {{ $('Read Settings').first().json['Opt-out EN'] }}
Return JSON: subject (max 7 words), body.

parameters.content:
## Compliance gate
Plain JavaScript, no AI. Blocks: empty email, free/personal domain, opted-out, email or domain on the Suppression tab (İYS "ret" opt-outs and manual do-not-contact entries), email domain not matching website, country not in the allowed list (Turkey). İYS itself is not queried: Nil exports İYS opt-outs into the Suppression tab. Add more rules here after Nil confirms KVKK / İYS requirements.

## Settings, Suppression and extra columns
Settings: one row with columns Sender Name, Sender Title, Company Legal Name, Company Address, Opt-out TR, Opt-out EN, Nil Email. Optional: Sheet URL, HubSpot Monthly Limit (default 3000), HubSpot Pause Percent (default 80).
Suppression tab: Email | Domain | Reason | Date (one row per address or domain never to contact).
Leads needs a Draft Body EN column. Log tab: Timestamp | Workflow | Lead ID | Company | Step | Input | Output | Reason.

## Draft check, English copy, log
Plain code, no AI: every draft must contain the sender name, legal name, address, the opt-out sentence in its language, the data-source sentence, no links except the lead's website, no hype words, and nothing commercially sensitive (buyer or brand names, money, quantities, order/price/capacity/margin wording). Failures are saved as Compliance Status = "Needs fix" with reasons, for Nil to correct before approving.
"Translate to English" (Claude Haiku 5.5) then writes a plain English copy of Turkish drafts to the Draft Body EN column so Nil can compare; English drafts leave it empty. The compliance decision and the draft are appended to the Log tab.
